exam_structure.paper_name: Rome and its neighbours — Roman Depth Study
exam_structure.overview: Q11(a)–(c) Discrete factual knowledge (5m, AO1); Q12 What can we learn from Prescribed Source/Passage (5m, AO3); Q13 How accurate is the Prescribed Source/Passage presentation (5m, AO3); Q14 Second-order concept explanation (10m: 5 AO1 + 5 AO2 — zero source reliability needed); Q15* Evaluative essay analysing Prescribed Ancient Sources + own knowledge (20m: 5 AO1 + 5 AO2 + 10 AO3).

literary: Cassius Dio, Roman History, XLII 44–45; XLIII 27
archaeological: Relief portraits of Cleopatra and Caesarion from Dendera
Coin of Cleopatra and Caesarion minted in Cyprus
Silver denarius of Antony and Cleopatra minted in 32, declaring Antony's conquest of Armenia and giving Cleopatra's title as 'queen of kings and of her sons who are kings' (British Museum)

sections.title: Key Topic 1: Ptolemaic Egypt, Upbringing & Julius Caesar (69–47 BC)

topics.title: 1.1 Family, Education, Character and Roman Clientage
points: Cleopatra's family and Macedonian heritage; her likely education and upbringing; her character as depicted in the sources, including her charm, her humour, and her courage
Rome's relationship with client states and attitude to foreigners; the importance of Egypt for Rome economically and politically; overview of Rome's involvement with Egypt in the 60s and 50s BC
prescribedSetSources: Coin of Ptolemy Auletes, British Museum
Head of Cleopatra as a young woman, British Museum

topics.title: 1.2 Accession, Civil War with Ptolemy XIII and Sibling Rivalry
points: The death of Ptolemy XII and Cleopatra's first years as queen; civil war between Cleopatra and Ptolemy XIII; Cleopatra's relationship with her brothers and Arsinoe

topics.title: 1.3 Meeting Caesar, Alexandrian War and Birth of Caesarion
points: Cleopatra's initial meeting with Caesar and his decision to support her; Cleopatra's personal and political relationship with Caesar and its impact on both Rome and Egypt; the birth of Caesarion

sections.title: Key Topic 2: Queen of Egypt, Isis Persona & Reception in Rome (47–44 BC)

topics.title: 2.1 Graeco-Egyptian Persona, Isis Promotion and Archaeology
points: Her Graeco-Egyptian public persona and representation in the archaeological sources; the promotion of Isis as her patron goddess and the rationale for this
prescribedSetSources: Relief portraits of Cleopatra and Caesarion from Dendera
Coin of Cleopatra and Caesarion minted in Cyprus
Coin of Cleopatra, with distinctive hairstyle and hooked nose, British Museum

topics.title: 2.2 Domestic Rule, Egyptian Subjects and Territorial Ambition
points: Cleopatra's relationship with her subjects; the expansion of Egyptian territory under Cleopatra

topics.title: 2.3 Cleopatra's Visit to Rome and Caesar's Assassination
points: Cleopatra's visit to Rome and her reception

sections.title: Key Topic 3: Cleopatra, Mark Antony & the Donations of Alexandria (44–32 BC)

topics.title: 3.1 Mark Antony's Position and the Meeting at Tarsus (41 BC)
points: Mark Antony's position in Roman politics after Caesar's death; Cleopatra's meeting with Mark Antony at Tarsus

topics.title: 3.2 Alliance, Eastern Territories and Octavia
points: The development of the political and personal relationship between Cleopatra and Mark Antony and its significance for both Egypt and Rome

topics.title: 3.3 Donations of Alexandria and Breakdown with Octavian
points: The role played by Cleopatra in the breakdown of Mark Antony and Octavian's relationship, including the Donations of Alexandria
prescribedSetSources: Silver denarius of Antony and Cleopatra minted in 32, declaring Antony's conquest of Armenia and giving Cleopatra's title as 'queen of kings and of her sons who are kings'

sections.title: Key Topic 4: War with Octavian, Actium & the Deaths in Alexandria (32–30 BC)

topics.title: 4.1 Causes of War and Preparations for Actium
points: Causes of the war between Octavian and Antony/Cleopatra; preparations for the battle

topics.title: 4.2 The Battle of Actium: Roles, Outcome and Competing Views
points: Key events of the battle, including the roles of Octavian, Agrippa, Mark Antony and Cleopatra; the outcome and the reasons for it as described by the sources; different views of the battle in the sources

topics.title: 4.3 Fall of Alexandria, Suicides and Significance for Octavian
points: Impact of the battle on Cleopatra's and Antony's careers; the method of Cleopatra's suicide and reasons for her actions; Mark Antony's suicide; the significance of the suicides for Octavian
